paper_title: Search for oscillations of fundamental constants using molecular spectroscopy
notes: Scalar (dilaton-like) UDM search with molecular iodine spectroscopy. Curve is the coupling to the fine-structure constant, panel (a) of Fig. 4 (dadme.pdf in e-print), extracted from the vector PDF: combined boundary of the excluded (shaded) region from Experiment A (red, ~10 Hz-1e5 Hz) and Experiment B (blue, 1e5 Hz-1e8 Hz). Mass from Compton freq via m_eV = 4.13567e-15 * f_Hz. The two experiments overlap in mass near ~4e-10 eV; both branches retained, hence the small non-monotonic step there (Expt A rising near its Nyquist edge, Expt B more sensitive above it). Convention: paper defines alpha(phi)=alpha(1 - d_alpha phi/M_Pl) with reduced M_Pl=2.4e18 GeV (Eq.3); canonical Damour-Donoghue d_e uses kappa=sqrt(4pi)/M_Pl_full, giving d_e = sqrt(2) * d_alpha. Applied factor sqrt(2). Curves are for the standard galactic UDM halo scenario (rho_DM=0.3 GeV/cm^3, page 3), 95% detection threshold (Fig.2b). NOTE the paper's own headline result is the FIRST bound on the QCD-sector (gluon+quark) combination Q_N.d (Fig.3), which has no clean canonical plane; the paper also reports d_me (panel b). d_alpha (=this plane) chosen as the main electromagnetic result because Expt A is dominantly alpha-sensitive (cavity R_alpha=1). The paper's limits are mostly weaker than existing bounds except in narrow bands (10-50 Hz, 5-10 kHz, 5-100 MHz).
